66: /** Decode all modifier properties into ngui inputs (reads the node's signals). */
67: export function buildMods(node: PathlandNode): NguiMods {
68:   const mods: NguiMods = {};
69: 
70:   const padding = buildPadding(node);
71:   if (padding) {
72:     mods.padding = { paddingAreas: padding };
73:   }
74:   const color = node.color(PROPERTY.COLOR);
75:   if (color !== undefined) {
76:     mods.color = argbToRgba(color);
77:   }
78:   const background = node.color(PROPERTY.BACKGROUND_COLOR);
79:   if (background !== undefined) {
80:     mods.background = { color: argbToRgba(background) };
81:   }
82:   const border = buildBorder(node);
83:   if (border) {
84:     mods.border = border;
85:   }
86:   const radius = node.f32(PROPERTY.BORDER_RADIUS);
87:   if (radius !== undefined && radius > 0) {
88:     mods.rounding = { radius };
89:   }
90:   const opacity = node.f32(PROPERTY.OPACITY);
91:   if (opacity !== undefined) {
92:     mods.opacity = opacity;
93:   }
94:   const font = buildFont(node);
95:   if (font.size || font.weight || font.family) {
96:     mods.font = font;
97:   }
98:   const frame = buildFrame(node);
99:   if (frame) {
100:     mods.frame = frame;
101:   }
102:   const flex = buildFlex(node);
103:   if (flex) {
104:     mods.flex = flex;
105:   }
106:   const lineLimit = node.f32(PROPERTY.LINE_LIMIT);
107:   if (lineLimit !== undefined) {
108:     mods.lineLimit = lineLimit;
109:   }
110:   return mods;
111: }
112: 
113: /** Stack spacing → ngui `[gap]` (px). */
114: export function stackGap(node: PathlandNode): number | undefined {
115:   return node.f32(PROPERTY.SPACING);
116: }
117: 
118: /** Stack cross-axis alignment → ngui `[alignment]` (ui-hstack / ui-vstack). */
119: export function stackAlignment(node: PathlandNode): NguiStackAlignment | undefined {
120:   const wire = node.f32(PROPERTY.ALIGNMENT);
121:   return wire === undefined ? undefined : nguiStackAlignment(wire);
122: }

124: /** Overlap alignment → ngui `[alignment]` (ui-zstack, broad `Alignment`). */
125: export function zstackAlignment(node: PathlandNode): NguiAlignment | undefined {
126:   const wire = node.f32(PROPERTY.ALIGNMENT);
127:   if (wire === undefined) {
128:     return undefined;
129:   }
130:   switch (Math.round(wire)) {
131:     case ALIGNMENT.LEADING: return 'leading';
132:     case ALIGNMENT.TRAILING: return 'trailing';
133:     default: return 'center';
134:   }
135: }
136: 
137: /** Text alignment → ngui `[multilineTextAlignment]`. */
138: export function textAlignment(node: PathlandNode): NguiTextAlignment | undefined {
139:   const wire = node.f32(PROPERTY.TEXT_ALIGNMENT);
140:   return wire === undefined ? undefined : nguiTextAlignment(wire);
141: }
142: 
143: /** Checked state (SELECTED) for toggles/checkboxes. */
144: export function checked(node: PathlandNode): boolean {
145:   const bits = node.props().get(PROPERTY.SELECTED);
146:   return bits !== undefined && bits !== 0;
147: }
148: 
149: /** Whether the node should be hidden (`VISIBLE = 0`). */
150: export function hidden(node: PathlandNode): boolean {
151:   const visible = node.f32(PROPERTY.VISIBLE);
152:   return visible !== undefined && visible === 0;
153: }
154: 
155: /** A slider's numeric range (VALUE/MIN_VALUE/MAX_VALUE, defaults 0/0/1). */
156: export function slider(node: PathlandNode): { value: number; min: number; max: number } {
157:   const min = node.f32(PROPERTY.MIN_VALUE) ?? 0;
158:   const max = node.f32(PROPERTY.MAX_VALUE) ?? 1;
159:   const value = node.f32(PROPERTY.VALUE) ?? min;
160:   return { value, min, max };
161: }
162: 
163: function buildPadding(node: PathlandNode): PaddingArea[] | undefined {
164:   const uniform = node.f32(PROPERTY.PADDING);
165:   const top = node.f32(PROPERTY.PADDING_TOP);
166:   const right = node.f32(PROPERTY.PADDING_RIGHT);
167:   const bottom = node.f32(PROPERTY.PADDING_BOTTOM);
168:   const left = node.f32(PROPERTY.PADDING_LEFT);
169:   if (uniform === undefined && top === undefined && right === undefined
170:       && bottom === undefined && left === undefined) {
171:     return undefined;
172:   }
173:   const areas: PaddingArea[] = [];
174:   if (uniform !== undefined && top === undefined && right === undefined
175:       && bottom === undefined && left === undefined) {
176:     areas.push({ edge: 'All', gap: uniform });
177:     return areas;
178:   }
179:   const pushEdge = (edge: PaddingArea['edge'], value: number | undefined) => {
180:     const gap = value ?? uniform;
181:     if (gap !== undefined) {
182:       areas.push({ edge, gap });
183:     }
184:   };
185:   pushEdge('Top', top);
186:   pushEdge('Trailing', right);
187:   pushEdge('Bottom', bottom);
188:   pushEdge('Leading', left);
189:   return areas;
190: }
191: 
192: function buildBorder(node: PathlandNode): BorderOptions | undefined {
193:   const width = node.f32(PROPERTY.BORDER_WIDTH);
194:   if (width === undefined) {
195:     return undefined;
196:   }
197:   const edgesBits = node.props().get(PROPERTY.BORDER_EDGES) ?? BORDER_EDGE.ALL;
198:   const colorBits = node.color(PROPERTY.BORDER_COLOR);
199:   const borderAreas: BorderArea[] = [];
200:   if (edgesBits === BORDER_EDGE.ALL) {
201:     borderAreas.push({ side: 'All', width });
202:   } else {
203:     if (edgesBits & BORDER_EDGE.TOP) borderAreas.push({ side: 'Top', width });
204:     if (edgesBits & BORDER_EDGE.BOTTOM) borderAreas.push({ side: 'Bottom', width });
205:     if (edgesBits & BORDER_EDGE.LEADING) borderAreas.push({ side: 'Left', width });
206:     if (edgesBits & BORDER_EDGE.TRAILING) borderAreas.push({ side: 'Right', width });
207:   }
208:   return {
209:     borderAreas,
210:     ...(colorBits !== undefined ? { color: argbToRgba(colorBits) } : {}),
211:   };
212: }
213: 
214: function buildFont(node: PathlandNode): { size?: string; weight?: string; family?: string } {
215:   const font: { size?: string; weight?: string; family?: string } = {};
216:   const size = node.f32(PROPERTY.FONT_SIZE);
217:   if (size !== undefined) {
218:     font.size = `${size}px`;
219:   }
220:   const weight = node.f32(PROPERTY.FONT_WEIGHT);
221:   if (weight !== undefined) {
222:     font.weight = cssFontWeight(weight);
223:   }
224:   const family = node.strings().get(PROPERTY.FONT_FAMILY);
225:   if (family) {
226:     font.family = family;
227:   }
228:   return font;
229: }
230: 
231: function buildFrame(node: PathlandNode): FrameOptions | undefined {
232:   const width = node.f32(PROPERTY.WIDTH);
233:   const height = node.f32(PROPERTY.HEIGHT);
234:   const frame: { width?: string; height?: string } = {};
235:   if (width !== undefined && width > 0) {
236:     frame.width = `${width}px`;
237:   }
238:   if (height !== undefined && height > 0) {
239:     frame.height = `${height}px`;
240:   }
241:   return frame.width || frame.height ? frame : undefined;
242: }
243: 
244: function buildFlex(node: PathlandNode): FlexOptions | undefined {
245:   const width = node.f32(PROPERTY.WIDTH);
246:   const height = node.f32(PROPERTY.HEIGHT);
247:   if (width === SIZE.FILL) {
248:     return { grow: 1 };
249:   }
250:   if (height === SIZE.FILL) {
251:     return { grow: 1, basis: '100%' };
252:   }
253:   return undefined;
254: }

257: function nguiStackAlignment(wire: number): NguiStackAlignment {
258:   switch (Math.round(wire)) {

260:     case ALIGNMENT.TRAILING: return 'trailing';

262:     default: return 'center';
263:   }
264: }

270:     case ALIGNMENT.TRAILING: return 'trailing';

272:   }
273: }

276: function cssFontWeight(wire: number): string {
277:   switch (Math.round(wire)) {
278:     case FONT_WEIGHT.LIGHT: return '300';
279:     case FONT_WEIGHT.MEDIUM: return '500';
280:     case FONT_WEIGHT.SEMIBOLD: return '600';
281:     case FONT_WEIGHT.BOLD: return 'bold';

288:   const a = (argb >>> 24) & 0xff;

291:   const b = argb & 0xff;

3: /**
4:  * The `PLPL` network batch codec — the TypeScript mirror of the Java
5:  * `com.pathland.view.transport.FrameCodec` and the Rust `pathland_core_transport`.
6:  *
7:  * Batch wire format (both directions share the header):
8:  *
9:  * ```
10:  * magic "PLPL" (u32 LE) | version (u16) | flags (u16) | frameCount (u32)
11:  * | opcodeCount (u32) | opcodes (16 B × count) | stringsLen (u32) | string bytes
12:  * ```
13:  *
14:  * Frames are self-contained: `SET_TEXT` / STRING-valued `SET_PROPERTY` reference
15:  * entries in the batch's own string section by *relative* offset.
16:  */
17: export const BATCH_MAGIC = 0x504c_504c; // "PLPL"
18: export const BATCH_VERSION = 1;
19: export const HOST_TO_GUEST = 0x0001;
20: export const HEADER_BYTES = 16;
21: 
22: const encoder = new TextEncoder();
23: const decoder = new TextDecoder();
24: 
25: /** Decode a `PLPL` batch into a frame (opcodes + string section). */
26: export function decodeFrame(bytes: Uint8Array): Frame {
27:   if (bytes.byteLength < HEADER_BYTES) {
28:     throw new Error('batch truncated');
29:   }
30:   const view = new DataView(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset, bytes.byteLength);
31:   if (view.getUint32(0, true) !== BATCH_MAGIC) {
32:     throw new Error('bad batch magic');
33:   }
34:   if (view.getUint16(4, true) !== BATCH_VERSION) {
35:     throw new Error('unsupported batch version');
36:   }
37:   const opcodeCount = view.getUint32(12, true);
38:   const opcodesEnd = HEADER_BYTES + opcodeCount * 16;
39:   if (opcodesEnd + 4 > bytes.byteLength) {
40:     throw new Error('batch truncated (opcodes)');
41:   }
42:   const opcodes: Opcode[] = new Array(opcodeCount);
43:   for (let i = 0; i < opcodeCount; i++) {
44:     const pos = HEADER_BYTES + i * 16;
45:     opcodes[i] = new Opcode(
46:       view.getUint8(pos),
47:       view.getUint8(pos + 1),
48:       view.getUint16(pos + 2, true),
49:       view.getUint32(pos + 4, true),
50:       view.getUint32(pos + 8, true),
51:       view.getUint32(pos + 12, true),
52:     );
53:   }
54:   const stringsLen = view.getUint32(opcodesEnd, true);
55:   const stringsStart = opcodesEnd + 4;
56:   if (stringsStart + stringsLen > bytes.byteLength) {
57:     throw new Error('batch truncated (strings)');
58:   }
59:   const strings = bytes.subarray(stringsStart, stringsStart + stringsLen);
60:   return new Frame(opcodes, strings);
61: }
62: 
63: /** Read a length-prefixed string (`[u32 len][bytes]`) at a relative offset. */
64: export function stringAt(strings: Uint8Array, offset: number): string {
65:   const view = new DataView(strings.buffer, strings.byteOffset, strings.byteLength);
66:   const len = view.getUint32(offset, true);
67:   return decoder.decode(strings.subarray(offset + 4, offset + 4 + len));
68: }

70: /**
71:  * Encode a frame (or host→guest event batch) as a `PLPL` byte array.
72:  * `flags` selects the direction (`HOST_TO_GUEST` for events).
73:  */
74: export function encodeBatch(
75:   opcodes: Opcode[],
76:   strings: Uint8Array,
77:   flags = 0,
78: ): Uint8Array {
79:   const opcodesEnd = HEADER_BYTES + opcodes.length * 16;
80:   const out = new Uint8Array(opcodesEnd + 4 + strings.byteLength);
81:   const view = new DataView(out.buffer);
82:   view.setUint32(0, BATCH_MAGIC, true);
83:   view.setUint16(4, BATCH_VERSION, true);
84:   view.setUint16(6, flags, true);
85:   view.setUint32(8, 0, true); // frameCount
86:   view.setUint32(12, opcodes.length, true);
87:   for (let i = 0; i < opcodes.length; i++) {
88:     const pos = HEADER_BYTES + i * 16;
89:     const op = opcodes[i];
90:     view.setUint8(pos, op.category);
91:     view.setUint8(pos + 1, op.command);
92:     view.setUint16(pos + 2, op.flags, true);
93:     view.setUint32(pos + 4, op.a, true);
94:     view.setUint32(pos + 8, op.b, true);
95:     view.setUint32(pos + 12, op.c, true);
96:   }
97:   view.setUint32(opcodesEnd, strings.byteLength, true);
98:   out.set(strings, opcodesEnd + 4);
99:   return out;
100: }

102: /** A growable string-section writer returning each entry's relative offset. */
103: export class StringSectionWriter {
104:   private readonly bytes: number[] = [];
105: 
106:   /** The byte length of the string section so far. */
107:   size(): number {
108:     return this.bytes.length;
109:   }
110: 
111:   /** Append a length-prefixed UTF-8 string; returns its relative offset. */
112:   push(text: string): number {
113:     const offset = this.bytes.length;
114:     const utf8 = encoder.encode(text);
115:     this.bytes.push(utf8.length & 0xff, (utf8.length >>> 8) & 0xff,
116:       (utf8.length >>> 16) & 0xff, (utf8.length >>> 24) & 0xff);
117:     for (const b of utf8) {

119:     }
120:     return offset;
121:   }

10:  * Mutable fields are Angular signals so frame deltas re-render only the
11:  * affected nodes (ngui is signal-driven and zoneless).

15:   /** Text set via `STYLE::SET_TEXT`. */
16:   readonly text = signal<string | null>(null);
17:   /** Raw wire values (`propertyId → bits`) for non-STRING properties. */
18:   readonly props = signal<Map<number, number>>(new Map());
19:   /** Resolved `STRING`-typed properties (`propertyId → text`). */
20:   readonly strings = signal<Map<number, string>>(new Map());

29:   }

43: /** The renderer's retained tree: applies `TREE`/`STYLE` opcodes in place. */
44: export class RetainedTree {
45:   private readonly nodes = new Map<number, PathlandNode>();
46: 
47:   /** The first node created (id 1 for the Java emitter). */
48:   get rootId(): number | null {
49:     return this.nodes.has(1) ? 1 : null;
50:   }
51: 
52:   node(id: number): PathlandNode | undefined {
53:     return this.nodes.get(id);
54:   }
55: 
56:   has(id: number): boolean {
57:     return this.nodes.has(id);
58:   }
59: 
60:   /** Apply a self-contained frame, mutating the retained tree. */
61:   applyFrame(frame: Frame): void {
62:     for (const op of frame.opcodes) {
63:       switch (op.category) {
64:         case CATEGORY.TREE:
65:           this.applyTree(op.command, op);
66:           break;
67:         case CATEGORY.STYLE:
68:           this.applyStyle(op.command, op, frame);
69:           break;
70:         default:
71:           break;
72:       }
73:     }
74:   }

76:   private applyTree(command: number, op: { a: number; b: number; c: number }): void {
77:     switch (command) {
78:       case TREE.CREATE_NODE:
79:         this.nodes.set(op.a, new PathlandNode(op.a, op.b & 0xffff));
80:         break;
81:       case TREE.DELETE_NODE:
82:         this.nodes.delete(op.a);
83:         break;
84:       case TREE.INSERT_CHILD: {
85:         const parent = this.nodes.get(op.a);
86:         if (parent) {
87:           parent.children.update((kids) => [...kids, op.b]);
88:         }
89:         break;
90:       }
91:       case TREE.REMOVE_CHILD: {
92:         const parent = this.nodes.get(op.a);
93:         if (parent) {
94:           parent.children.update((kids) => kids.filter((k) => k !== op.b));
95:         }
96:         break;
97:       }
98:       case TREE.MOVE_CHILD: {
99:         const parent = this.nodes.get(op.a);
100:         if (parent) {
101:           parent.children.update((kids) => {
102:             const next = kids.filter((k) => k !== op.b);
103:             const index = Math.min(op.c, next.length);
104:             next.splice(index, 0, op.b);
105:             return next;
106:           });
107:         }

116:       if (node) {

118:       }
119:       return;
120:     }

122:       return;
123:     }

125:     if (!node) {

127:     }
128:     const property = op.b & 0xffff;
129:     const valueType = (op.b >>> 16) & 0xff;
130:     if (valueType === VALUE_TYPE.STRING) {
131:       node.strings.update((m) => new Map(m).set(property, frame.stringAt(op.c)));
132:     } else {

134:     }
135:   }
136: }

142:   return view.getFloat32(0, true);

I have a complete picture now. Here's my research and proposed plan.

## Findings

**`pathland-demo-views`** today: 3 views (`CounterView` root, `CounterControls`, `NameField`) + 1 test. Both demos hardcode `new CounterView()` as the session root (`SessionApp.java`). The DSL now has a full control/modifier surface (Phase 1–3), and the Java `HtmlRenderer` (SSR) renders all of them — so a kitchensink can be built purely from `View` composition + `State<T>` fields (auto-wired by the annotation processor).

**Critical blocker for the browser**: Phase 1 renumbered component IDs, but the **Angular client is not synced**:
- `lib/angular/src/app/pathland/core/protocol.ts` still uses legacy IDs (`TEXT=0x0003, VSTACK=0x0002, …`), `FONT_WEIGHT` compact 0–4 scale, stale `PADDING_STYLE`.
- The demos now emit spec IDs, so the Angular `kindOf()` returns `'unknown'` for every node → **the current demos already render as blank children-only trees in the browser** (SSR HTML still works).
- New controls (Toggle, Picker, ColorPicker, DatePicker, TextEditor, Stepper…) have no `mapping.ts`/`node.component.html` cases, and the client sends `POINTER_UP` for toggles while the Java `Toggle` registers a `valueInput` (`VALUE_CHANGED`) — so browser toggles wouldn't update state.
- The vanilla `app.js` fallback in both demos has the same issues (toggle → POINTER_UP, no select/textarea/color/date handlers).

## Proposed plan

### Part 1 — `pathland-demo-views` kitchensink (primary deliverable)
New custom views in `com.pathland.demo`, one class per section (each with `State<T>` fields using **explicit keys** to avoid cross-section key collisions):

| View | Demonstrates |
|------|-------------|
| `KitchenSinkView` (new root) | `ScrollView` + `VStack` of sections + header/footer |
| `SectionCard` (reusable wrapper) | composition + a custom card (`background`, `border`, `cornerRadius`, `padding`) |
| `CounterSection` | `Button`, `Stepper`, `State<Integer>` (+ computed label) |
| `TextFieldSection` | `TextField`, `TextEditor`, `State<String>` |
| `ToggleSection` | `Toggle` in all 3 styles (Switch/Checkbox/Button), `State<Boolean>` |
| `ValueControlsSection` | `Slider`, `Stepper`, `Gauge`, `ProgressView`, linked `State<Float>` |
| `PickerSection` | `Picker` (segmented + menu), `Menu` with actions, `State<Integer>` |
| `ColorSection` | `ColorPicker`, `Color` view, `Rectangle` (SHAPE), `State<Color>` |
| `DateSection` | `DatePicker`, `State<Integer>` (days) |
| `LayoutSection` | `Grid`, `LazyVStack`, `HStack`+`Spacer`, `ZStack`, `Divider` |
| `TextStylesSection` | text modifiers (weight/italic/underline/strikethrough/textCase/kerning/…) |
| `AppearanceSection` | border/shadow/opacity/clipShape/rotation/scaleEffect/zIndex |

- New test `KitchenSinkViewTest`: mount against `InMemoryStateStore`, assert the emitted frame contains the expected component types + persisted values, and drive a toggle/slider `valueInput` through the registry (same pattern as `CounterViewTest`).
- Switch both demos' `SessionApp` roots to `new KitchenSinkView()`.
- Keep `CounterView`/`CounterControls`/`NameField` (still referenced by `CounterViewTest`).

### Part 2 — renderer sync so the demo actually renders in the browser (recommended; without it the browser shows nothing)
- **Angular** (`lib/angular`): renumber `protocol.ts` COMPONENT/PROPERTY/EVENT/LISTENER to spec + `FONT_WEIGHT` 100–900; apply `STYLE::SET_DATE` in `retained-tree.ts`; extend `mapping.ts` `kindOf` + `node.component.html` cases for all new components; route toggle/stepper/picker/colorPicker via `VALUE_CHANGED`, textEditor via `TEXT_CHANGED`, datePicker via new `DATE_CHANGED` encoder; update `mapping.spec.ts`/`core.spec.ts`.
- **app.js** (both demos): fix toggle→`VALUE_CHANGED`, add stepper/select/textarea/color/date handlers.
- **Verification**: `npm test` + `ng build` in `lib/angular`; the same JDK-22-preview test harness for Java (JDK 25 unavailable here).

## Questions before I finalize

Plan confirmed. Here's the final implementation plan.

## Part 1 — `pathland-demo-views` kitchensink

**New files** in `com.pathland.demo` (one custom `View` class per section, each with `State<T>` fields using explicit keys):

1. `SectionCard.java` — reusable wrapper: title + `Divider` + styled card (`background`, `border`, `cornerRadius`, `padding`).
2. `KitchenSinkView.java` — new root: `ScrollView` → `VStack` of all sections + header/footer.
3. `CounterSection.java` — `State<Integer> count` ("count"), `Stepper` for step size, increment/decrement/reset `Button`s, computed label.
4. `TextFieldSection.java` — `State<String> name` ("name"), `TextField` + `TextEditor`, computed label.
5. `ToggleSection.java` — `State<Boolean>` ×3 (`dark`/`notify`/`bold`), all three `ToggleStyle`s (Switch/Checkbox/Button) + computed summary.
6. `ValueControlsSection.java` — `State<Float> value` ("value"), `Slider`, `Stepper`, `Gauge`, `ProgressView` all bound to it, computed label.
7. `PickerSection.java` — `State<Integer> selection` ("selection"), `Picker` (Segmented + Menu styles), `Menu` with actions.
8. `ColorSection.java` — `State<Color> accent` ("accent"), `ColorPicker` + `Color` view swatch + `Rectangle`.
9. `DateSection.java` — `State<Integer> days` ("days"), `DatePicker`, computed date label.
10. `LayoutSection.java` — `Grid`, `LazyVStack`, `HStack`+`Spacer`, `ZStack` badge, `Divider`.
11. `TextStylesSection.java` — one `Text` row per modifier (fontWeight/italic/underline/strikethrough/textCase/kerning/tracking/lineLimit/fontDesign).
12. `AppearanceSection.java` — `border`/`shadow`/`opacity`/`clipped`/`clipShape`/`rotation`/`scaleEffect`/`zIndex` on a styled card.

**Modified**: 
- `pathland-demo-views/pom.xml` description (optional).
- `KitchenSinkViewTest.java` (new): mount against `InMemoryStateStore`, assert emitted component types (TOGGLE/SLIDER/PICKER/COLOR_PICKER/DATE_PICKER present in the frame), assert persisted values, drive a `valueInput` via the registry.
- Quarkus `SessionApp.java` + Spring `SessionApp.java`: `new CounterView()` → `new KitchenSinkView()`.
- `status.md` (demo-views has none — add/update the AGENTS-referenced per-project status; check if one exists).

Keep `CounterView`/`CounterControls`/`NameField` + `CounterViewTest` as-is.

## Part 2 — Renderer sync (browser)

**Angular** (`lib/angular`):
- `core/protocol.ts`: renumber `COMPONENT` to spec ranges; add `COLOR/SHAPE/DIVIDER/PROGRESS_VIEW/GAUGE/ZSTACK/TEXT_EDITOR/TOGGLE/STEPPER/DATE_PICKER/PICKER/MENU/COLOR_PICKER/LAZY_*`; add properties `SHAPE_KIND/TOGGLE_STYLE/PICKER_STYLE/PROGRESS/IS_INDETERMINATE/STEP_VALUE/COLOR_VALUE/DATE_PICKER_MODE/SELECTION/TINT`; add `STYLE.SET_DATE`, events `FOCUS_CHANGED/EDITING_CHANGED/SUBMIT/SCROLL/WHEEL/DATE_CHANGED`, listener bits 5–9; `FONT_WEIGHT` → 100–900; drop stale `PADDING_STYLE`.
- `core/retained-tree.ts`: apply `STYLE.SET_DATE` (days/millis on node).
- `ngui/mapping.ts`: `kindOf` for all new components; `TOGGLE_STYLE` → switch/checkbox; helpers for stepper/gauge/progress/date; `cssFontWeight` for the 100–900 scale.
- `ngui/node.component.html`: new `@case` blocks — `color` (greedy div), `shape`, `divider` (hr), `progressView`, `gauge`, `textEditor` (textarea), `stepper`, `toggle` (ui-toggle/ui-checkbox by style), `picker` (select), `menu`, `colorPicker` (input color), `datePicker` (input date), `lazyVStack/HStack` → ui-stack, `lazyVGrid/HGrid` → ui-grid.
- `ngui/node.component.ts` + `core/event-encoder.ts` + `ngui/session.service.ts`: route toggle/stepper/picker/colorPicker via `valueChanged`, textEditor via `textChanged`, datePicker via a new `dateChanged` encoder (`DATE_CHANGED`, B=days, C=millis).
- Update `mapping.spec.ts` + `core.spec.ts` to the new IDs.

**app.js** (both demos): toggle → `VALUE_CHANGED` (0/1), add handlers for stepper buttons, `select`, `textarea`, `input[type=color]`, `input[type=date]`; textEditor → `TEXT_CHANGED`.

## Verification
- Java: compile + run the full `pathland-view`/`pathland-render-html`/`pathland-demo-views` test suite via the JDK-22-preview harness (JDK 25 unavailable here), including the generated `_StateBinder` (compile `pathland-view-processor` + run `javac -processorpath`).
- Angular: `npm test` (vitest) + `npx ng build` in `lib/angular`.
- Rust: `cargo test` (should stay at 190).
- Update `status.md` for any module touched.

# pathland-demo-views — implementation status

**Last updated:** August 29, 2026

The framework-agnostic shared demo views (`com.pathland.demo`), consumed by the
Quarkus and Spring Boot demos. Uses `State` fields wired by the
`pathland-view-processor` annotation processor.

## Implemented

- **`KitchenSinkView`** (the demo root): a scrollable column of every protocol
  section, mounted by both demos' `SessionApp`.
- **Sections** (each a custom `View`):
  - `SectionCard` — reusable titled/bordered/rounded section wrapper.
  - `CounterSection` — `State<Integer>` + `Button` + `Stepper`.
  - `TextFieldSection` — `TextField` + `TextEditor` on one `State<String>`.
  - `ToggleSection` — `Toggle` in all three `ToggleStyle`s.
  - `ValueControlsSection` — `Slider`/`Stepper`/`Gauge`/`ProgressView` on one
    `State<Float>`.
  - `PickerSection` — `Picker` (Segmented + Menu) + `Menu`.
  - `ColorSection` — `ColorPicker` + `Color` as a View + reactive `Rectangle`.
  - `DateSection` — `DatePicker` bound to days-since-epoch.
  - `LayoutSection` — `Grid`/`LazyVStack`/`HStack`+`Spacer`/`ZStack`/`Divider`.
  - `TextStylesSection` — text-formatting modifiers.
  - `AppearanceSection` — border/shadow/opacity/transform/hidden/z-index.
- **Legacy views kept**: `CounterView`, `CounterControls`, `NameField` (still
  covered by `CounterViewTest`).

## Not implemented / gaps

- The browser experience depends on the Angular renderer and the demos'
  `app.js`, which are synced separately (see `lib/angular` and the demo
  `src/main/resources`).

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-demo-views` (needs JDK 25) — `CounterViewTest`,
`KitchenSinkViewTest` (mount + persistence + input routing).

# lib/angular — implementation status

**Last updated:** August 29, 2026

The Angular 21 **browser renderer** mapping opcode frames onto the
`@apaq/ngui` design system (`ui-vstack`/`ui-text`/`ui-button`/…). Protocol
contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Protocol constants** (`core/protocol.ts`): synced to the spec's grouped
  component ranges (`TEXT 0x01`, `COLOR 0x03`, `VSTACK 0x10`, `HSTACK 0x11`,
  `TOGGLE 0x24`, `SLIDER 0x25`, `COMMENT 0x7F`, …), full property catalog
  (incl. `TINT`/`SHAPE_KIND`/`TOGGLE_STYLE`/`PICKER_STYLE`/`SELECTION`/
  `COLOR_VALUE`/`DATE_PICKER_MODE`/…), `STYLE::SET_DATE`, the full event
  catalog (`KEY_*`, `FOCUS_CHANGED`, `EDITING_CHANGED`, `SUBMIT`, `SCROLL`,
  `WHEEL`, `DATE_CHANGED`), listener bits 0–9, and `FONT_WEIGHT` on the spec's
  100–900 scale.
- **Decoder** (`core/decoder.ts`): `PLPL` batch decode (`decodeFrame`),
  `HOST_TO_GUEST` direction, `TEXT_CHANGED` string-section resolution.
- **Retained tree** (`core/retained-tree.ts`): applies `TREE`/`STYLE` deltas
  including `STYLE::SET_DATE` (node date state).
- **Event encoder** (`core/event-encoder.ts`): host→guest event batches —
  pointer, `VALUE_CHANGED` (f32 or raw bits), `TEXT_CHANGED` with string
  offsets, `DATE_CHANGED` (days/millis).
- **ngui mapping** (`ngui/mapping.ts`): all spec components — stacks (incl.
  `LAZY_*`), `ZSTACK`, `GRID`, `SCROLLVIEW`, `TEXT`, `BUTTON`, `IMAGE`,
  `COLOR`, `SHAPE`, `DIVIDER`, `SPACER`, `TEXT_FIELD`, `TEXT_EDITOR`,
  `TOGGLE` (`TOGGLE_STYLE` → switch/checkbox/button), `SLIDER`, `STEPPER`,
  `PICKER`, `MENU`, `COLOR_PICKER`, `DATE_PICKER`, `PROGRESS_VIEW`, `GAUGE`;
  `hidden` reads the `VISIBLE` `U8` bit.
- **Renderer** (`ngui/node.component.ts|html`): one case per kind — ngui views
  for the supported ones, native HTML elements for the rest (textarea, select,
  color/date inputs, range, progress, gauge, stepper); input routed back as
  `VALUE_CHANGED`/`TEXT_CHANGED`/`DATE_CHANGED`.
- **Session** (`ngui/session.service.ts`): connects to `/ws`, the server
  replays the mount frame on connect (`SessionApp`).

## Not implemented / gaps

- No `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID` gating (the Java emitter routes by node id via
  `RenderResult` registries).
- `app.spec.ts` is an `ng test` (Karma/Jasmine) spec; the unit specs
  (`core.spec.ts`, `mapping.spec.ts`) run under vitest.

## Verified by

`npx vitest run` (18 unit tests) + `ng build` (template/TS compilation).

1: # Pathland Protocol
2: 
3: > A cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol inspired by SwiftUI
4: 
5: ## Overview
6: 
7: Pathland is a **protocol-first** UI framework for **retained-mode UI** with
8: multiple renderer backends. It's inspired by SwiftUI's declarative syntax, but
9: designed to be **language-agnostic** and **platform-agnostic**.
10: 
11: As of August 2026 the core is a **Rust opcode engine**. It emits the
12: application's **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
13: padding, alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared
14: linear memory. Each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that
15: platform's **native elements** (GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the
16: browser, HTML server-side) and those native elements lay themselves out.
17: 
18: On desktop the engine runs **natively**: other languages drive it through the
19: flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-view-native`) over a zero-copy shared ring and render
20: through the shared GTK renderer (`pathland-render-gtk`).
21: 
22: **The engine does not compute layout and does not emit rects.** It describes
23: *what* the UI is, never *where* it is. Emission is **diff-based and reactive**:
24: change detection is fine-grained and signal-based — a signal bound to a node's
25: text or a property re-emits only that node's deltas, so only the things that
26: actually changed emit opcodes and an unchanged tree emits zero opcodes.
27: 
28: ## The Three Elements
29: 
30: Pathland is composed of three elements. They are the vocabulary the whole
31: project speaks, so they are settled and used consistently:
32: 
33: ```
34: ┌────────────────────┐        ┌─────────────────────┐
35: │ 1. Retained UI     │        │ 3. Renderer         │
36: │ the app's UI tree  │────┐   │ maps opcodes onto   │
37: │ (any language,     │    │   │ native elements +   │
38: │  any platform)     │    │   │ event reporting     │
39: └────────────────────┘    │   └───────────▲─────────┘
40:                          │                │
41: ┌────────────────────┐    │                │
42: │ 2. Opcode engine   │◄───┘                │
43: │ reconciles + emits │─────────────────────┘
44: └────────────────────┘
45: ```
46: 
47: 1. **Retained UI** — the application's canonical retained UI tree. It is the
48:    single source of truth, owned by the application. It can be authored in
49:    **any language on any platform**: Rust, Java, Swift, C#, C, TypeScript —
50:    desktop, mobile, or embedded — through a generated DSL or the flat native C
51:    ABI.
52: 2. **Opcode engine** — the producer: reconciles the retained tree and emits it as
53:    fixed **16-byte opcodes** using fine-grained, signal-based change detection: a
54:    signal bound to a node's text or a property re-emits only that node's deltas,
55:    so only the things that actually changed emit and an unchanged tree emits zero
56:    opcodes. The engine is language-independent — the same opcode stream serves
57:    every renderer. It spans a pure protocol core (`pathland-core`) and a
58:    retained-tree emitter (`pathland-engine`).
59: 3. **Renderer** — consumes the opcode stream and maps it onto that platform's
60:    **native elements**, and reports raw inputs back as events. It is a pure
61:    function of the opcode stream (stateless) and never retains application
62:    state. *"Host" and "driver" are roles a renderer plays: it runs inside a
63:    host and is pumped by a driver — they are not separate elements.* The same
64:    opcode stream targets **different UI systems**: a GTK4 renderer on desktop,
65:    an AppKit/SwiftUI renderer on macOS, a WinUI renderer on Windows, an LVGL
66:    renderer on embedded, a DOM renderer in the browser.
67: 
68: The opcodes are carried from the engine to the renderer by a transport (a
69: zero-copy shared-memory ring on desktop/native, a serialized network batch for
70: remote/browser); transport is an implementation detail, not a fourth element.
71: 
72: ## Core Principles
73: 
74: - **Protocol-first**: standardized, open protocol for UI components, events, and raw inputs
75: - **16-byte opcodes**: every instruction is a fixed 16 bytes — cache-line aligned, deterministic, linear decode
76: - **Declarative, not positioned**: the engine emits structure + constraint properties (spacing, padding, alignment); native renderers compute positions
77: - **Native elements everywhere**: GTK4 widgets, DOM elements, HTML — never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent
78: - **Reactive emission**: fine-grained, signal-based change detection — only the nodes that actually changed emit opcodes; steady state emits zero
79: - **Command-based**: UI updates are tree mutations (CREATE_NODE, DELETE_NODE, INSERT_CHILD, MOVE_CHILD, …), never serialized trees
80: - **Stateless renderers**: renderers are pure functions of the opcode stream; they retain only their own rendered output, never application state
81: - **Zero-copy**: ring and arena are plain regions of shared linear memory
82: - **Single-producer / single-consumer**: guest engine produces; host renderer consumes
83: - **Hand-written Java DSL**: the SwiftUI-like view DSL lives as a reusable Java library (`com.pathland.view`), not generated code — one ergonomic surface for desktop, server (Spring/Quarkus), and embedded hosts
84: 
85: ## Documentation
86: 
87: ### Specification
88: 
89: - [Opcode Protocol](./spec/OPCODE.md) — **Primary specification** — fixed 16-byte opcodes, ring buffer, arena, reactive emission, design tokens
90: - [Primitive Views](./spec/PRIMITIVES.md) — the primitive views the protocol supports (SwiftUI groupings), with protocol component IDs and status
91: - [Core Modifiers](./spec/MODIFIERS.md) — the core modifiers (protocol `STYLE` properties), SwiftUI-style, with property IDs and status
92: - [Core Events](./spec/EVENTS.md) — the core events (raw inputs), SwiftUI-style, with event command IDs and listener bits
93: - [Conformance Test Vectors](./spec/CONFORMANCE.md) — golden byte arrays for validating implementations
94: 
95: ## Rust Workspace
96: 
97: The implementation is under [`lib/rust/`](./lib/rust/):
98: 
99: | Crate | Element | Responsibility |
100: |-------|---------|----------------|
101: | `pathland-view` | Retained UI | SwiftUI-style view DSL: VStack/HStack/Text/Button + chainable modifiers building a `pathland-engine::Node` tree (`no_std`) |
102: | `pathland-core` | Opcode engine | Protocol core: fixed 16-byte opcode, ring buffer, bump arena, events, memory layout, Guest/Host/Frame surface (`no_std`, zero-alloc) |
103: | `pathland-engine` | Opcode engine | Emitter: retained tree types (`Node`/`Component`) + diff-based reactive emission + reactive **signals** (moved out of `pathland-core`) |
104: | `pathland-core-transport` | Opcode engine | Transport: shared-memory ring + network batch encode/decode + batching policy (`std`) |
105: | `pathland-render-gtk` | Renderer | GTK4 renderer (rlib + cdylib): opcode frames → native GTK widgets, incrementally |
106: | `pathland-render-html` | Renderer | HTML renderer: maps opcode frames onto declarative HTML (flex stacks, spans, buttons) as a pure function of the stream — the server-side/remote target |
107: | `pathland-view-native` | Retained UI projection | Native C-ABI shim + `NativeHost`: flat world over a zero-copy shared ring (Swift/Java/C#…) |
108: | `pathland-core-capi` | Opcode engine | Minimal shared-memory ring C ABI (`libpathland_core`): create/destroy, ring push, frame boundaries, arena alloc, zero-copy read, event drain/send |
109: | `pathland-render-gtk-demo` | Demo | Rust GTK4 demo: authors the DSL, renders through `pathland-render-gtk` (no GTK APIs) |
110: 
111: ## Java Libraries
112: 
113: The reusable, framework-agnostic Java libraries live under [`lib/java/`](./lib/java/)
114: (Maven reactor, `org.pathland`, Java 25+):
115: 
116: | Module | Package | Responsibility |
117: |--------|---------|----------------|
118: | `pathland-view` | `com.pathland.view` | SwiftUI-like view DSL (`View`, `VStack`, `Text`, `Button`, …), Angular-style signals/computed/effects (`com.pathland.view.signal`), fine-grained opcode emitter (`com.pathland.view.emit`), wire codec (`com.pathland.view.transport`), lazy FFM ring interop (`com.pathland.view.ffm`), cross-platform state (`com.pathland.view.state`: `StateStore`/`PersistentState`/`State`) |
119: | `pathland-view-processor` | `com.pathland.processor` | JSR 269 annotation processor: generates `<View>_StateBinder` for `State` fields (auto-keyed by field name) |
120: | `pathland-render-html` | `com.pathland.render.html` | Pure-function HTML renderer over the opcode stream (SSR) with `data-pathland-id` hydration |
121: | `pathland-state-redis` | `com.pathland.state.redis` | Redis-backed `StateStore` over Lettuce (Spring/Quarkus/desktop) |
122: | `pathland-demo-views` | `com.pathland.demo` | Shared demo views (`CounterView`/`CounterControls`/`NameField`) declaring `State` fields |
123: | `pathland-quarkus-demo` | `com.pathland.quarkus` | Quarkus SSR + WebSocket demo consuming the libraries |
124: | `pathland-spring-boot-demo` | `com.pathland.spring` | Spring Boot SSR + WebSocket demo consuming the same libraries |
125: 
126: The same `com.pathland.view` DSL (and `State` fields) runs unchanged on a Spring Boot
127: app, a Quarkus app, or a desktop app; a desktop host pushes opcodes into the Rust ring via
128: FFM (`pathland_ring_buffer_push`), while a server emits self-contained frames over WebSocket.
129: 
130: ### Build & run the Java libraries
131: 
132: ```bash
133: # Rust ring C ABI (only needed for the desktop FFM path)
134: cd lib/rust && cargo build -p pathland-core-capi
135: 
136: # Build + test the whole Java reactor (needs JDK 25: maven.compiler.release=25)
137: export JAVA_HOME=<jdk-25-home>
138: cd lib/java && mvn -q install
139: 
140: # Run the Quarkus SSR + WebSocket demo in dev mode (hot reload)
141: cd lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo && mvn quarkus:dev      # http://localhost:8080
142: 
143: # ...or run the packaged runner
144: cd lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo
145: mvn -q package
146: java -jar target/quarkus-app/quarkus-run.jar   # http://localhost:8080
147: 
148: # Run the Spring Boot SSR + WebSocket demo (same shared views)
149: cd lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo
150: mvn -q package
151: java -jar target/pathland-spring-boot-demo-0.1.0.jar   # http://localhost:8080
152: ```
153: 
154: The libraries require **Java 25+** (`ScopedValue` is final only in JDK 25, JEP 506),
155: **Quarkus ≥ 3.18** (dev mode's class-file reader must understand Java 25), and
156: **Spring Boot ≥ 3.5** (Java 25 support).
157: 
158: ### Run tests
159: 
160: ```bash
161: cd lib/rust && cargo test
162: cd lib/java && mvn test
163: ```
164: 
165: ### Run the GTK desktop demo (native, zero-copy shared ring)
166: 
167: ```bash
168: cd lib/rust && PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo run -p pathland-render-gtk-demo
169: ```
170: 
171: ## Angular Renderer (@apaq/ngui)
172: 
173: The browser also has a declarative renderer: an **Angular application** (under
174: [`lib/angular/`](./lib/angular/)) that maps the opcode stream onto the
175: **[@apaq/ngui](https://github.com/Apaq/ngui)** design system — `ui-vstack`/
176: `ui-hstack`/`ui-text`/`ui-button`/… views and `[padding]`/`[color]`/`[font]`/…
177: modifiers — instead of hand-written `app.js` DOM patches. It connects to the
178: Pathland `/ws` socket (the server replays the full mount frame on connect, so no
179: SSR pre-step is needed), decodes `PLPL` frames, and renders ngui views. See
180: [`lib/angular/README.md`](./lib/angular/README.md).
181: 
182: ## Components & Properties
183: 
184: Component and property IDs are defined in `pathland-core`'s
185: [`constants.rs`](./lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs),
186: documented in [OPCODE.md](./spec/OPCODE.md), and catalogued by category in
187: [PRIMITIVES.md](./spec/PRIMITIVES.md) (component types), [MODIFIERS.md](./spec/MODIFIERS.md)
188: (properties), and [EVENTS.md](./spec/EVENTS.md) (events). Component types
189: include `TEXT`, `BUTTON`, `VSTACK`, `HSTACK`, `SPACER`, and more; stack
190: constraint properties (`SPACING`, `ALIGNMENT`, …) drive native layout, styling
191: modifiers (`PADDING`, `COLOR`, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, …) decorate any view, and
192: `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` use `-1` = FILL, `-2` = HUG_CONTENT.
193: 
194: ## Design Tokens
195: 
196: The renderer owns default token values; the application owns overrides.
197: Tokens are identified by dot-separated paths (`color.primary`, `space.2`) and
198: referenced via the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type or overridden globally with
199: `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`. See [Design Token System](./spec/OPCODE.md#design-token-system).
200: 
201: ## Roadmap (POC Goals)
202: 
203: See the GitHub issues (#12, #13, #15, #16, #18):
204: 
205: 1. **16-byte opcode engine** — done
206: 2. **Core components & modifiers in Rust** (SwiftUI-like API) — done
207: 3. **Opcode transport layer** (shared memory + network batch + native C-ABI shim) — done
208: 4. **Rust desktop app with GTK4 renderer** (native shared ring) — done
209: 5. **Native Java library set** (hand-written `com.pathland.view` DSL + signals/computed/effects + reusable HTML renderer + state stores) — done
210: 6. **Quarkus SSR + WebSocket demo** (SSR HTML via `pathland-render-html` + live 16-byte opcode deltas) — done
211: 
212: ## Versioning
213: 
214: Pathland follows **Semantic Versioning** (Major.Minor.Patch). The wire protocol
215: version is 1 (see [OPCODE.md](./spec/OPCODE.md)).
216: 
217: ## License
218: 
219: Pathland is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details.

1: # Pathland Protocol
2: 
3: > A cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol for declarative, retained-mode UI
4: >
5: > **Status: proof of concept.** Not production software — the wire format and APIs may change before 1.0.
6: 
7: ## Overview
8: 
9: Pathland is a **protocol-first** UI framework for **retained-mode UI** with
10: multiple renderer backends. It offers a declarative, retained-mode view API
11: (SwiftUI-shaped in ergonomics) designed to be **language-agnostic** and
12: **platform-agnostic**.
13: 
14: As of August 2026 the core is a **Rust opcode engine**. It emits the
15: application's **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
16: padding, alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared
17: linear memory. Each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that
18: platform's **native elements** (GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the
19: browser, HTML server-side) and those native elements lay themselves out.
20: 
21: On desktop the engine runs **natively**: other languages drive it through the
22: flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-view-native`) over a zero-copy shared ring and render
23: through the shared GTK renderer (`pathland-render-gtk`).
24: 
25: **The engine does not compute layout and does not emit rects.** It describes
26: *what* the UI is, never *where* it is. Emission is **diff-based and reactive**:
27: change detection is fine-grained and signal-based — a signal bound to a node's
28: text or a property re-emits only that node's deltas, so only the things that
29: actually changed emit opcodes and an unchanged tree emits zero opcodes.
30: 
31: ## Project Status
32: 
33: **Proof of concept.** Pathland is a working reference implementation for
34: validating the protocol, not production software. The 16-byte opcode engine,
35: the Rust and Java DSLs, the GTK4 / HTML / Angular renderers, and the

content.text:
Audit complete. Here's the focused assessment of the Angular renderer (`lib/angular`) against `spec/`.

## Not in sync with the spec

**Missing protocol surface (ignored at the wire):**
1. `STYLE::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (0x02) and the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (0x08) — the renderer is documented "design-token-driven" but never reads token overrides.
2. `META::RESET` (0x01) — the retained tree is never cleared on reset (stale nodes persist).
3. `META::ENVIRONMENT` (0x02) — ignored.

**Component mapping deviations:**
4. `COMMENT` (0x7F) → `kindOf` returns `'comment'`, but there is **no `@case 'comment'`** in `node.component.html`, so it falls to `@default` and renders its children. Spec: COMMENT is opaque/debug, renderers must ignore it (no native element).
5. `IMAGE` (0x02) reads `[src]="n.text()"` (`SET_TEXT`), but spec says the source is the `IMAGE_SOURCE` property (0x1002, STRING).

**Modifier/property gaps (spec properties present in `protocol.ts` but not mapped to ngui):**
6. Text-format: `FONT_STYLE` (italic), `FONT_DESIGN`, `FONT_WIDTH`, `KERNING`, `TRACKING`, `BASELINE_OFFSET`, `LINE_SPACING`, `TEXT_CASE`, `UNDERLINE`, `STRIKETHROUGH` — none wired (ngui `FontOptions` exposes `style`/`lineHeight` but `buildFont` ignores them).
7. Layout: `OFFSET_X/Y`, `POSITION_X/Y`, `FIXED_SIZE_*`, `LAYOUT_PRIORITY`, `ASPECT_RATIO`, `CONTENT_MODE`, `MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR`; `frame` min/ideal/max (`MIN_WIDTH`…) and `alignment` (ngui `FrameOptions` supports them) — not applied.
8. Effects/transform: `SHADOW_*`, `BLUR_RADIUS`, `SATURATION`, `CONTRAST`, `BRIGHTNESS`, `GRAYSCALE`, `HUE_ROTATION`, `COLOR_MULTIPLY`, `COLOR_INVERT`, `ROTATION_DEGREES`, `SCALE`, `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` — none mapped.
9. Interaction: `ENABLED` (disabled), `Z_INDEX`, `TINT`, `CONTROL_SIZE`, `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING` — not mapped.

**Control semantics not fully honored:**
10. `TOGGLE_STYLE=Button` renders a `ui-button` but doesn't reflect the checked state.
11. `PICKER_STYLE` (Segmented/Wheel/RadioGroup) — all collapse to a `<select>`; only Menu is right.
12. `TEXT_FIELD` `IS_SECURE` (SecureField) — not masked.
13. `SLIDER` `STEP_VALUE` — not applied (no `step` on the range input).
14. `DATE_PICKER` `DATE_PICKER_MODE` (Time/DateAndTime) and `SET_DATE` millis-of-day — date-only.
15. `SHAPE` `SHAPE_KIND` Capsule/Ellipse/Path — only Circle/Rectangle/RoundedRectangle approximated.
16. `MENU` — items are statically `display:none`; no open/close, and the chosen action index is never reported (`VALUE_CHANGED`).

**Event catalog gaps (client → server):**
17. Only `POINTER_UP`, `VALUE_CHANGED`, `TEXT_CHANGED`, `DATE_CHANGED` are encoded. Missing: `POINTER_DOWN`, `POINTER_MOVE` (drag/hover basis), `KEY_DOWN/UP`, `FOCUS_CHANGED`, `EDITING_CHANGED`, `SUBMIT`, `SCROLL`, `WHEEL`.

## Does not work yet

1. **`app.spec.ts` is broken** — uses Jasmine `describe`/`beforeEach` globals, but the runner is vitest (Angular 21 `@angular/build:unit-test`) with no globals; fails with `describe is not defined`. Only `core.spec.ts`/`mapping.spec.ts` run.
2. **No vitest config** — no `vitest.config.ts`/globals, so `npx vitest run` reports "1 failed" (picks up `app.spec.ts`); the `ng test` builder and the loose vitest invocation disagree.
3. **`IMAGE`** won't display anything sourced via `IMAGE_SOURCE`.
4. **Design tokens** are ignored — hardcoded defaults (gauge `#2196F3`, border color, etc.) instead of session-token resolution.
5. **`META::RESET`** — a server reset is dropped.
6. **Drag/hover/keyboard/focus/scroll/submit** — no client-side production of these events, so the app can't react to them.
7. **Text-format/effect modifiers** render as if absent (italic/underline/strikethrough/shadow/rotation/… have no visual effect).
8. **Stepped slider / segmented/wheel picker / secure field / time mode** all degrade to their simplest form.

## Proposed remediation (priority order)

- **P1 — wire correctness:** fix `COMMENT` (ignore, render nothing), `IMAGE` → `IMAGE_SOURCE`, handle `META::RESET` (clear tree), `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (store token overrides).
- **P2 — controls:** `TOGGLE_STYLE=Button` checked state, `SLIDER` step, `IS_SECURE` mask, `PICKER_STYLE` variants, `DATE_PICKER_MODE` + millis, `SHAPE` Capsule/Ellipse/Path, `MENU` open/close + `VALUE_CHANGED` reporting.
- **P3 — modifiers:** map text-format (`FONT_STYLE`→`style`, `LINE_SPACING`→`lineHeight`, underline/strikethrough via decorators), frame min/ideal/max + alignment, effects/transform (shadow/rotation/scale at least).
- **P4 — events:** add `POINTER_DOWN/MOVE`, `KEY_*`, `FOCUS_CHANGED`, `EDITING_CHANGED`, `SUBMIT`, `SCROLL`, `WHEEL` to `event-encoder.ts` + `session.service.ts`, and wire them from the relevant native elements.
- **P5 — test infra:** add a `vitest.config.ts` with `globals: true` (or convert `app.spec.ts` to vitest imports) so `ng test`/`vitest` are green and consistent.

content.text:
Yes. `META::RESET` is part of the spec.

From `spec/OPCODE.md` §"META (0x04)" (lines 345–350):

| Command | Value | Description |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| `RESET` | `0x01` | Host must clear all rendered output |
| `ENVIRONMENT` | `0x02` | Viewport size in logical points (host → guest) |

Note the subtlety worth flagging for the Angular renderer specifically: `META` is categorized **"Both"** direction (OPCODE.md line 93), and the spec's `RESET`/`ENVIRONMENT` are written from the host → guest perspective ("Host must clear all rendered output", "Viewport size (host → guest)"). For the browser renderer, "host" = the renderer itself, so `RESET` means the renderer must clear its own retained tree/rendered output. The Angular `RetainedTree` currently only consumes `TREE` and `STYLE` categories and ignores `META` entirely — so a `RESET` opcode would be silently dropped, leaving stale nodes. So yes: it's spec'd, and the renderer gap I flagged (not handling `META::RESET` → clear the retained tree) is a real spec deviation.

In my earlier P1 list I wrote "handle `META::RESET` (clear tree)" — that stands. `META::ENVIRONMENT` (viewport size) is also spec'd but only meaningful if the renderer reports the viewport to the guest; the Angular renderer has no such channel today, so it's a lower-priority gap.

487: ## Design Token System
488: 
489: ### Core Principle
490: 
491: > **The renderer owns the defaults. The application owns the overrides.**
492: 
493: This ensures a native look-and-feel by default and cross-platform consistency when the application overrides tokens.
494: 
495: ### Responsibilities
496: 
497: | Aspect | Owner | Responsibility |
498: |--------|-------|----------------|
499: | **Default Token Values** | Renderer | Define platform-appropriate defaults for all standard tokens |
500: | **Token Overrides** | Application | Specify overrides for cross-platform consistency |
501: | **Token Resolution** | Renderer | Resolve final token values (override or default) |
502: | **Platform Adaptation** | Renderer | Adapt default token values to platform conventions |
503: 
504: ### Token Identification
505: 
506: Tokens are identified by **dot-separated string paths** (e.g. `color.primary`, `space.2`, `font.body`), case-sensitive, lowercase recommended. The `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (`0x08`) references a token path stored in the arena; `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides a token's value globally.
507: 
508: ### Token Resolution Algorithm
509: 
510: ```
511: FUNCTION resolveToken(tokenPath: string) -> PropertyValue:
512:     IF applicationOverrides.has(tokenPath):
513:         RETURN applicationOverrides[tokenPath]
514:     ELSE IF rendererDefaults.has(tokenPath):
515:         RETURN rendererDefaults[tokenPath]
516:     ELSE IF hasParentToken(tokenPath):
517:         RETURN resolveToken(getParentPath(tokenPath))
518:     ELSE:
519:         RETURN getFallbackValue(tokenPath)
520: ```
521: 
522: ### Renderer Responsibilities
523: 
524: The renderer MUST:
525:

content.text:
All five phases done, each committed. During P2 I also applied your **ngui-only rule**: the renderer uses only `@apaq/ngui` components, and any protocol component the design system lacks renders a temporary ngui-styled **"not implemented" placeholder** instead of raw HTML.

## Commits
- `d3223c1` **P1 — wire correctness**: `COMMENT` ignored (no native element), `IMAGE` src from `IMAGE_SOURCE`, `META::RESET` clears the retained tree (+tokens/viewport), `META::ENVIRONMENT` viewport, `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides stored with override→default→parent-path resolution.
- `7549948` **P2 — ngui-only controls**: `ui-text-area` (TextEditor), `ui-select`/`ui-radio-group`/`ui-button` (Picker by `PICKER_STYLE`), `ui-menu`+`[triggerFor]` (Menu → `onSelect`→`VALUE_CHANGED`), `ui-date-picker` (DATE mode), `ui-rectangle`/`ui-circle` (Color view + all SHAPE kinds), `ui-button` for `TOGGLE_STYLE=Button` (checked `✓`). Placeholders for `SLIDER`, `STEPPER`, `PROGRESS_VIEW`, `GAUGE`, `COLOR_PICKER`, `DIVIDER`, `SecureField`, `PICKER::Wheel`, `DATE_PICKER::Time/DateAndTime`, `SHAPE::Path`.
- `16a4981` **P3 — modifiers → ngui**: `[shadow]`, `[rotationEffect]`, `[underline]`, background CSS filter (blur/saturation/contrast/brightness/grayscale/hue-rotate/invert), font `style`/`lineHeight`, frame min/max + alignment.
- `9ca9f58` **P4 — full event catalog**: pointer down/move/up, `KEY_*`, focus/editing/submit/scroll/wheel encoders + `session.service` senders (wire-complete; ngui only produces the outputs it exposes).
- `f5f3196` + `9faa0fd` **P5 — test infra**: `vitest.config.ts` for the unit specs; `ng test` (Angular unit-test builder) is the canonical runner.

## Verification
- `ng test` → **25 tests / 3 files** green (incl. TestBed `app.spec.ts`).
- `npx vitest run` (in `lib/angular`) → **24 tests** green.
- `ng build` → passes.
- Java 40 + Rust 190 tests untouched and still green.
